shots.line: This twenty-one-year-old became a millionaire with just one website... and he didn't even sell a single product.
shots.scene: sunset town square: a young student stands in front of a giant billboard made of a million colourful ad pixels; bills flutter, a counter races to $1,000,000

shots.line: See, Alex Tew was a broke student in England who needed money for university. So he came up with an idea that sounded completely ridiculous.
shots.scene: a cosy student room in England at sunset, LONDON poster; Alex sits broke at his laptop, then a lightbulb idea flashes

shots.line: He built a website with exactly one million pixels... and started selling them. One pixel, one dollar. Businesses could buy a spot and put their ad on it.
shots.scene: close on Alex's monitor: an empty white grid titled The Million Dollar Homepage — $1 per pixel; the first small colourful ads pop in
night in the dorm: Alex stares at a nearly empty pixel grid, crickets chirp

shots.line: But then the newspapers picked up the story... and suddenly, everyone wanted a piece of his website.
shots.scene: golden town square: newspapers with headlines spin in; reporters with cameras flash; crowds point at the giant pixel billboard

shots.line: Pixels were selling like crazy. When only the last thousand were left, Alex put them up for auction... and they sold for thirty-eight thousand dollars.
shots.scene: the website fills at crazy speed with colourful ads; zoom on the last empty 1,000 pixels — AUCTION — gavel — $38,100

shots.line: In just a few months, his website made over one million dollars.
shots.scene: sunset dorm: Alex jumps for joy while hundred-dollar bills rain down; the counter passes one million dollars

shots.line: And the craziest part? The website is still online today. He didn't invent anything new. He just figured out how to turn attention into money.
shots.scene: the real Million Dollar Homepage (photo) in a clean browser frame, slow zoom across the ads — still online today; attention = money
